text:
Priya: RFC follow-up — sketched two approaches for SDK pagination+retries across Python/TS/Go. Option A = expose a shimless, resume-able iterator in each language (iterator is part of public surface). Option B = keep simple page/token APIs in SDKs and implement resume/retry logic in a transport proxy/adapter layer. Curious tradeoffs and real-world gotchas.

Matt: I lean shimless for developer ergonomics. Most of our users expect to `for item in client.list_x()` style loops. If retry+resume is built into iterator, common case is simpler. :+1:

Carlos: Biggest worry is cross-protocol tokens. Backend APIs return different resume tokens (cursor vs opaque token). Transport can't invent a token if server doesn't send it. For proxy to work we need strict server guarantees.

Evan: Also language ergonomics matter. Go iterators are stateful `Next() (Item, error)` loops; TS likes async generators; Python wants synchronous + async variants. A single "shimless" contract across all three needs careful shape choices.

Lauren: Proposal for compromise: define a tiny canonical contract (ResumeToken as opaque string, `resume(token)` API) and then each language binding adapts to idioms. Example sketches: 

Python: 
```
it = client.list_documents_iter(page_size=100)
for doc in it:
    process(doc)
# resume later
it2 = client.list_documents_iter(resume_token=it.resume_token)
```

TS: 
```ts
for await (const doc of client.listDocuments({ pageSize: 100 })) {
  process(doc)
}
const resumed = client.listDocuments({ resumeToken: token })
```

Go: 
```go
it := client.ListDocuments(ctx, &ListOpts{PageSize:100})
for it.Next() {
  doc := it.Item()
}
// resume using token string
it2 := client.ListDocuments(ctx, &ListOpts{ResumeToken: token})
```

Matt: That feels reasonable. Key is metadata: iterator should expose a small, language-agnostic `resume_token` that the transport/backend understands. Then retried requests can supply it.

Carlos: For streaming endpoints (server-side streaming), resume semantics differ — sometimes you resume by replaying last-seen sequence number, other times you need server snapshot. We need to clearly annotate which endpoints support resume.

Anita: We should avoid breaking changes to existing page APIs. Suggest adding a v2 iterator surface (feature-flagged) and keep old `list_pages()` until we deprecate. Also document semver and compatibility expectations.

Priya: Agreed. Operational concerns: if we put retry logic in transport proxy (Option B), we centralize backoff, jitter, and circuit-breaker policies — good for Private where customers run their own proxies. But hosted customers benefit more from SDK-level ergonomics (Option A).

Evan: Another runtime concern: KV cache/prefix caching interacts with resume tokens. If we auto-retry from transport with a different token, we might bypass cache and increase cost. Need telemetry to measure token churn and cache hits.

Matt: Suggested rollout plan: implement shimless iterators in SDKs (python/ts/go) but keep transport hooks for enterprise/private deployments. Start hosted beta, enable canary for 5% of traffic, measure failed resumes, token size, tail latency.

Lauren: Also add an opt-in `transparent_retries` flag in SDK config. Default = false for initial rollout. That lets callers opt-in to SDK-level retry/resume behavior.

Anita: Action items I can take: 1) Draft API shapes for Python/TS/Go (small PRs), 2) Add matrix of endpoints that can support resume, 3) Telemetry events for resume attempts and outcomes.

Priya: Thanks — that's a good division. I'll open an RFC follow-up summarizing: API shapes, rollout plan, telemetry, and default config. @Matt can you help with the canary pipeline? @ops-bot will post deploy events. :rocket:

ops-bot: [deploy] canary rollout started for "shimless-iterators" on hosted (5% traffic).

Matt: Happy to own canary. I'll add dashboards for resume_success_rate, resume_fail_reasons, token_length_hist.

Carlos: One minor nit — document expected idempotency of list endpoints. If server doesn't guarantee idempotency for list calls, resume semantics are undefined. Add that check before enabling `transparent_retries`.

Priya: Good point. We'll add a gating column in the endpoint matrix (idempotent? yes/no).

Lauren: Small UX note: when resume fails, iterator should surface a clear exception with server-side token info (not just opaque network error). Helps SRE debugging.

Evan: Agreed. And for Go/TS, include a small helper to convert token -> human-readable debug string when available.

Priya: OK — next steps: Anita drafts PRs for API shapes this week, I'll write the RFC follow-up and link code sketches, Matt will stand up canary dashboards. We'll reconvene in #eng-platform next Tuesday for a short sync. :calendar:

Matt: :thumbsup:

Anita: On it.
